differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.

T-2565's loggia, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): Glessner's front and the tree in front of 1808 hide the loggia; only the top of the balcony's south pedestal shows, so this view cannot judge its carving or columns.

T-2566's granite, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): the tree's crown covers the front's checker band and courses and Glessner's roof hides the bow; the north return's courses are T-2564's item above.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
The earlier low stone boundary replaces the generic iron fence with urns. Its exact post/rail sections remain reconstructed.

T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.
T-2578: this print does not resolve the corner behind the rear pinnacle (trees and grain); the stone parapet's stop there is ruled from the views that see it.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: Keith's front is foreshortened beyond reading the band's units.

T-2748 (the reviewer's reason for this verdict): this file is the owner's reproduction of the c. 1888 SW photograph, cropped (the crown above the third-storey lights is out of frame, so the pinnacles, the return's coping and the cowl are not shown here) and about a third of the blog copy's size, now on that view's re-fitted camera. In register, the third-storey lights, the bow and the north arris lie on the print's; the stoop does not, and reads here as it does in the c. 1888 view: its landing's pierced balustrade and the low round arch under its flight stand left of the render's (the arch at about x 296-305 against 310-321 at this file's scale) and the arch far lower than built. The record differs on that alone. T-2812 ruled it (tools/keith_c1888_stoop_read.py; docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/a18-gh-1800-block-looking-sw-c1888-stoop.json): the print draws the loggia's front at its built width (the deck front 85 px against 80, the pierced parapet 40 against 40, its shadowed north side beside it) displaced as one block about 35-40 px left and down, and no level camera holds that block and the crown together: fitted on the crown, every camera leaves the loggia 32-41 px off across and 29-49 px off down; fitted on both, the crown goes to 20 px and T-1883's south-corner grade point to 10-42 px. Only an eye 5-6 m up fits both (7.7 px RMS), and the print's own horizon refuses it: Glessner's two identical window grids scale about y 986, where that eye's horizon is y 734. The 1888 plate (its level fits have the pedestals' arrises and caps in them, 4.6-5.4 px RMS) and the 1965 slide (the shafts' and south pedestal's silhouettes, 3.4 px, the pedestal caps predicted within 3-4 px) place the loggia, its deck and its stair as built, with the plan's deck 2.7 m out; the plate draws the arch's crown at y 1728 against the built 1724, its void 10-15 px inside the built outline in its shadowed reveal. What this print shows of the arch is its head over a light band at y 1032 in front of it; where the block is displaced, the built crown lands on the print's (y 1009-1011 against 1012). So this print cannot place the stoop: a 35 px move would be about 0.9 m out from the front or 1.4 m south along it against three readings that hold it, and the stoop is not moved. With the stoop ruled, nothing this record names is open, and as T-2748 found everything else in register here, the verdict is matches.

T-2813: re-rendered with Keith's crown 0.16 m lower (the moulded course under the lattice 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, the checker and head bands unmoved); its camera re-solved on the moved crown controls (carried from the c. 1888 camera through its map, tools/keith_crown_resolve.py). Read again at the crown beside the previous render: the lattice, coping and pinnacles move a few pixels at this picture's scale and nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands as it was (matches).

T-2876: re-rendered on the GLB in the tree, T-2845's loggia (0.6 m pedestals at the first-floor plan's place, each pair's shafts 0.36 m apart, the flight 1.8 m clear and the stoop 0.15 m south), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia and flight (x 269-416, y 0-283); at this copy's size the loggia's pairs are a few pixels each and their move is below its grain, and it cannot read a rear row (not shown). Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict returns to matches.

T-2881: re-rendered on the loggia with its rear row built (a pedestal 0.6 m square against the wall behind each front one, carrying a pair of turned shafts 0.39 m off the wall at a 0.28 m pitch, their radii 0.78 of the front's, under a paired capital; tools/keith_loggia_rear_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-rear-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 335-364, y 181-240); at this copy's size the loggia's pairs are a few pixels each and the rear row is below its grain. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict returns to matches.

T-2882: re-rendered on the loggia with a respond on the wall behind each rear pair (a flat pier the rear pedestal's width, 0.25 m deep, from the pedestal's top to the ceiling; tools/keith_loggia_respond_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-respond-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 334-366, y 182-223); the rear row stands behind the respond's face, and this picture does not read the rear row, for the reason T-2881's item above gives, so it does not read the respond either. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands (matches).

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
